find: GRANT SELECT ON control_effect_intents TO control_room_task_coordinator;
replace: -- MUTATED: the coordinator's effect-intent read is removed
why: reconcileStalled reads effect intents to decide whether an outcome is uncertain; without the grant it fails 42501 for every eligible candidate on real PostgreSQL

replace: // MUTATED: the effect-intent read is undeclared, so the preflight and the role file disagree
why: the startup preflight declares exactly the coordinator grants the role files confer; dropping the declaration makes a correctly installed database fail its own preflight
a worker's in-flight lease leaves the active set at revocation, so the supervisor never sweeps it as a stall

find: const leaseMoved = await this.#moveOrAlready(tx, lease, "revoked", base);
why: the revoked lease really leaves state 'active'

find:
await this.#moveOrAlready(tx, attempt, "cancelled",
        { ...base, patch: { finishedAt: now, safeFailureCode: "worker_revoked" } }, "waiting");
why: the withdrawn attempt is cancelled rather than left leased

find:
await tx.query("DELETE FROM control_assignment_lease_scopes WHERE tenant_id=$1 AND lease_id=$2",
        [this.#tenantId, lease.id]);
why: the revoked lease releases its derived ownership scope, so later work in that project is not blocked

find: WHERE fc.tenant_id=$1 AND fc.worker_id=$2 AND l.state='active' ORDER BY fc.claimed_at LIMIT 50`,
replace: WHERE fc.tenant_id=$1 AND fc.worker_id=$2 ORDER BY fc.claimed_at LIMIT 50`,
why: the candidate window is bounded at 50 rows over an append-only claims table, so it must consider only still-active leases or 50 terminal claims crowd out the live one and the owner's revocation silently misses in-flight work

find:
WHERE a.tenant_id=$1 AND a.id=$2 AND a.state IN ('leased','running','waiting')
          AND j.state IN ('leased','running') AND l.state='active' AND l.expires_at<=$3
replace:
WHERE a.tenant_id=$1 AND a.id=$2 AND a.state IN ('leased','running','waiting','cancelled')
          AND j.state IN ('leased','running','orphaned') AND l.state='active' AND l.expires_at<=$3
why: reconcileAttempt re-checks the attempt and job states under FOR UPDATE, so a concurrent sweep cannot reconcile an attempt a revocation already cancelled; the binding predicate is l.state='active', which this widening leaves intact
the production driver sanitizes the SQLSTATE onto sqlState, so reading only code turns a scope collision into an opaque refusal
a claim overlapping a live ownership lease is the clean conflict it always was, not a crash
